prizes.motivation: for his investigations and discoveries in relation to tuberculosis
prizes.microscopy: Koch's proof that the tubercle bacillus causes tuberculosis included a method for staining the bacterium in diseased tissue so it could be seen under the microscope. The prize presentation also credits him with developing staining and microscopic investigation techniques early in his career.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1905 - Summary

prizes.motivation: in recognition of their work on the structure of the nervous system
prizes.microscopy: Golgi found that impregnating nervous tissue with silver nitrate stains only a few nerve cells black, so single cells and their processes stand out under the microscope. Cajal refined the method and, working at the microscope, drew thousands of detailed images of nervous tissue.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1906 - Summary

prizes.motivation: in recognition of his work on the role played by protozoa in causing diseases
prizes.microscopy: Laveran discovered the malaria parasite by examining fresh blood from patients, without stains, and seeing unfamiliar bodies inside and among the red blood cells. His own account describes the observation as made while examining the blood by microscope.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1907 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for his demonstration of the heterogenous nature of colloid solutions and for the methods he used, which have since become fundamental in modern colloid chemistry
prizes.microscopy: Zsigmondy devised the ultramicroscope, which lights the sample from the side, perpendicular to the viewing direction, so particles too small to resolve show up as bright points against a dark background. With it he showed that colloid solutions that look uniform in an ordinary microscope contain discrete particles of varying size. (The prize was awarded in 1926 as the 1925 prize.)

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1925 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for his work on the discontinuous structure of matter, and especially for his discovery of sedimentation equilibrium
prizes.microscopy: Perrin prepared emulsions of tiny gamboge spheres, checked under the microscope, and followed their Brownian movement and sedimentation. These measurements confirmed Einstein's theory of Brownian motion and gave new values of Avogadro's number.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1926 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for his demonstration of the phase contrast method, especially for his invention of the phase contrast microscope
prizes.microscopy: Transparent specimens shift the phase of light without changing its brightness, so they are nearly invisible in an ordinary microscope. Zernike's phase contrast method converts those phase shifts into differences in brightness, which made it possible to see unstained living cells.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1953 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for his invention and development of the holographic method
prizes.microscopy: Gabor first conceived holography as a way to improve electron microscope images: record the object's wave field with electrons as a hologram, then reconstruct it with visible light into a high-resolution image. The method later became general optical holography.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1971 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for their discoveries concerning the structural and functional organization of the cell
prizes.microscopy: Claude was among the first to apply the new electron microscope to animal cells, and he paired it with differential centrifugation to separate cell parts for chemical study. Palade continued this work and, among other findings, described the ribosomes on cell membranes. De Duve, who shared the prize, was the biochemist of the group (he discovered new organelles by cell fractionation).

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1974 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for his development of crystallographic electron microscopy and his structural elucidation of biologically important nucleic acid-protein complexes
prizes.microscopy: Klug combined electron microscopy with diffraction methods from X-ray crystallography to reconstruct three-dimensional structures from electron micrographs. His approach gave high-quality images at low radiation dose and without heavy metal stains, and he used it on viruses and chromatin.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1982 - Summary

prizes.motivation: Ruska: for his fundamental work in electron optics, and for the design of the first electron microscope; Binnig and Rohrer: for their design of the scanning tunneling microscope
prizes.microscopy: Ruska found that a short current-carrying coil can focus electrons the way a lens focuses light, and in 1933 he built an electron microscope that clearly outperformed the light microscope. Binnig and Rohrer built the scanning tunneling microscope in 1981: a sharp tip scanned over a surface resolves individual atoms.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1986 - Summary
Speed read: Beyond the realm of our senses

prizes.motivation: for their discoveries concerning genetic regulation of organ development and programmed cell death
prizes.microscopy: The worm C. elegans is transparent, so every cell division can be followed directly under the microscope. Sulston used this to map the complete cell lineage and noticed that certain cells always die at set times, which led to the work on programmed cell death. The press release says that combining genetics with cell divisions watched under the microscope started the prize-winning discoveries.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2002 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for their discoveries concerning magnetic resonance imaging
prizes.microscopy: Magnetic resonance imaging is not microscopy: it forms images of the body from the magnetic resonance of hydrogen nuclei. It appears here as a related imaging prize for comparison with optical and electron imaging.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2003 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for their discovery of the bacterium Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease
prizes.microscopy: Warren, a pathologist, saw small curved bacteria in stomach biopsies under his microscope and linked them to inflammation of the stomach lining. The press release lists silver staining of histological sections among the methods that, with endoscopy and culture, proved that H. pylori causes disease.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2005 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for the discovery and development of the green fluorescent protein, GFP
prizes.microscopy: GFP can be fused genetically to other proteins, so they glow and can be followed under the fluorescence microscope inside living cells and organisms without injecting any dye. It became a standard tagging tool, used for example to watch nerve cells develop or cancer cells spread.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2008 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for the invention of an imaging semiconductor circuit - the CCD sensor
prizes.microscopy: The CCD is an image sensor that turns light into a digital image, an array of photocells whose charge is read out pixel by pixel. CCD cameras, including electron-multiplying CCDs, became standard detectors for low-light fluorescence and super-resolution microscopy. (Kao shared the prize for optical fibres.)

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2009 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for the development of super-resolved fluorescence microscopy
prizes.microscopy: Abbe's 1873 limit held that optical microscopes could not resolve details finer than about 0.2 micrometres. Hell developed STED microscopy, demonstrated in 2000, and Betzig and Moerner, working separately, laid the foundation for single-molecule microscopy. Together these methods took fluorescence microscopy to the nanometre scale.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2014 - Summary
Popular information: How the optical microscope became a nanoscope

prizes.motivation: for his discoveries of mechanisms for autophagy
prizes.microscopy: Yeast cells are small and their inner structures are hard to see under the microscope. Ohsumi used yeast strains that could not break down material in the vacuole, so autophagosomes built up there and became visible under the microscope. This experiment showed that autophagy occurs in yeast and opened the way to his genetic screens.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2016 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for developing cryo-electron microscopy for the high-resolution structure determination of biomolecules in solution
prizes.microscopy: Biomolecules dry out in the vacuum of an electron microscope and are damaged by the beam. Henderson showed in 1990 that electron microscopy could solve a protein structure at atomic resolution. Frank developed image processing that merges many noisy 2D images into a sharp 3D structure, and Dubochet cooled water so fast around the sample that it vitrified (solidified without crystallizing), so biomolecules keep their natural shape in the vacuum.

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2017 - Summary

prizes.motivation: for the optical tweezers and their application to biological systems
prizes.microscopy: Optical tweezers use a focused laser beam to trap and move particles, viruses and living cells without harming them. Looking through a microscope, Ashkin found that particles caught in his laser trap were bacteria, and in 1987 he trapped living bacteria. The tweezers are now widely used to study the molecular machinery of life. (Mourou and Strickland shared the prize for high-intensity ultrashort laser pulses.)

sources.title: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2018 - Summary
